passages.title: Getting to yes
passages.text: It is often assumed that a successful negotiation ends with one winner and one loser. Experienced negotiators, however, would argue the opposite. What matters most is not how much you win, but whether both sides leave the table willing to work together again. The first step is to find common ground: shared interests that neither party is prepared to sacrifice. Once these have been identified, concessions become far easier to make, since each side can see what it stands to gain. Leverage still plays a role, of course. A buyer with several alternative suppliers is in a stronger position than one with none, and it would be naive to pretend otherwise. Yet using that leverage aggressively tends to backfire: the other party may agree to a deal today only to look for a way out of it tomorrow. Not only does a one-sided agreement damage trust, but it also makes future negotiations slower and more expensive. The most effective negotiators therefore treat disagreements as problems to be ironed out rather than battles to be won. Rarely do they reach an agreement in a single meeting, but when they do, it is one that both sides are willing to honor.

passages.title: A formal reply
passages.text: Thank you for your proposal regarding the new supply contract, which our team has now reviewed in detail. While we appreciate the effort that has gone into it, we are unable to accept the terms in their current form. The bottom line is that a price increase of this size would make the contract unprofitable for us, and we cannot see how it would benefit either party in the long run. That said, we remain keen to find a win-win solution. We would therefore like to request a meeting to discuss two possible alternatives: a longer contract at the current price, or a smaller increase in exchange for larger orders. We should also point out that the delivery schedule is a deal-breaker for us. Much as we value our relationship, we must stand firm on this point, as late deliveries would affect our own customers. Should you wish to purchase additional services, we would be happy to include them in the discussion. Please do not hesitate to contact me if you require any further information. We look forward to hearing from you.
